title: 1-byte read past the end of a 24-byte object
object: a, 24 bytes, the first of two consecutive st_alloc(24)
control: reads a[23] instead of a[24]; allocation traffic identical

asan.why: ASan keeps the request size, so offset 24 is in the right redzone on malloc and in the arena's 16-byte alignment slack (24..31) when the allocator unpoisons exactly n.

valgrind.why: Memcheck reports an invalid read only for an unaddressable byte; inside an arena every byte is addressable until a mempool request says otherwise.

hwasan.why: A 24-byte malloc block ends mid-granule, and HWASan's short-granule tagging stores the size in the last byte of the granule, so offset 24 is caught. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: LowFat's bounds are the SIZE CLASS, 32 bytes for a 24-byte request, so offset 24 is in bounds even on malloc. Documented sub-object imprecision, not an allocator effect: compare case 3, where the offset leaves the class.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc and arena; server run pending (A5)
